notes:
RULE 3 FINDING: overstock.com is live (not shut down, not a network redirect) but its category/product catalogue layer is the IDENTICAL underlying Bed Bath & Beyond / Beyond Inc. catalogue already fully extracted at S.N. 47 (pipeline/final_list_batch_sn41-50/c47.json, 78 leaf / 18 parent rows), not a genuinely separate Home Decor catalogue. Recorded qty:null / rows:[] rather than duplicating that extraction, per Rule 3's explicit instruction.

EVIDENCE (five independent signals, all pointing the same way):
1. DNS: `nslookup www.overstock.com` and `nslookup www.bedbathandbeyond.com` both resolve through the IDENTICAL Akamai edge alias chain (e3734.dsca.akamaiedge.net / CNAME target ds-cdn.overstock.com.edgekey.net) - same CDN/origin configuration for both domains.
2. Shared image CDN: product images on both domains are served from the same host ak1.ostkcdn.com/images/products/<numeric-id>/..., keyed by the identical numeric product-ID space (confirmed via each domain's own sitemap: api.overstock.com/sitemaps/overstock-v3/us/products1.xml and bedbathandbeyond.com/sitemaps/bedbathandbeyond/us/products2.xml both point at ak1.ostkcdn.com for their images).
3. Shared taxonomy ID space: overstock.com's own nav (captured via translate.goog server-rendered HTML) links to /c/mirrors/wall-mirrors?t=28409 and /c/home-decor?t=28396 - the exact same `t=28409` taxonomy ID that S.N. 47's c47.json already recorded for bedbathandbeyond.com's 'Wall Mirrors' row (qty 6898, same slug path mirrors/wall-mirrors), and t-values in the identical numeric neighborhood as BBB's other Home Decor nodes (t=28407 wall-shelves, t=28410 floor-mirrors, t=28412 wall-clocks). Two brands do not independently arrive at the same taxonomy-ID integers by coincidence - this is one shared category database.
4. DECISIVE: WebFetch (JS-rendered, i.e. what a real browser actually shows) of four separate overstock.com URLs - the homepage (https://www.overstock.com/), the roster's own assigned URL (https://www.overstock.com/Home-Garden/Home-Decor/248/cat.html), the Home Decor category (https://www.overstock.com/c/home-decor?t=28396), and the Wall Mirrors category (https://www.overstock.com/c/mirrors/wall-mirrors?t=28409) - ALL FOUR render with page title 'Bed Bath & Beyond | The Best Deals Online: Furniture, Bedding, Rugs, Kitchen Essentials & More' and Bed Bath & Beyond logo/header branding, not Overstock branding. The roster's exact assigned category URL literally renders as Bed Bath & Beyond.
5. BBB's own robots.txt (fetched last batch's S.N. 47 route) disallows /Garage-Automotive/* - a legacy Overstock-style top-level path grammar - showing BBB's routing config still recognizes and reserves the old Overstock URL taxonomy even though it is not linked from BBB's own nav; overstock.com's product sitemap uses that exact /<Dept-slug>/<product-slug>/<id>/product.html grammar.

NUANCE: a raw, non-JS server-rendered fetch of the bare overstock.com homepage via translate.goog (no live JS execution) still shows a legacy, unmigrated SEO <title> ('Shop Overstock for Furniture, Rugs & Stylish Outdoor Living.') and its own top nav linking to /c/furniture, /c/rugs, /c/lighting, /c/home-decor, /c/outdoor, plus footer links out to bedbathandbeyond.com/careers and bedbathandbeyond.com/partner (a cross-brand link bar, the same pattern S.N. 47 found linking BBB to containerstore.com). This is consistent with a domain mid-migration: the marketing/SEO shell on the homepage has not been fully repointed, but the actual product/category rendering layer (what WebFetch's JS-rendered pass shows, and what matters for this extraction) has already been consolidated onto the Bed Bath & Beyond brand and platform.

ACCESS ROUTE ATTEMPTED (for completeness, before reaching the Rule 3 conclusion): direct fetch of category pages 403s (Akamai). A 20-profile curl_cffi sweep (chrome99-131, chrome-android, safari15-18/ios, edge, firefox) got either a flat 403 or a 200 Akamai Bot-Manager behavioural-challenge interstitial (2598 bytes, 'sec-if-cpt-container') on every /c/ category URL tested - never real product content. translate.goog rendered the bare homepage successfully (200, real origin HTML) but returned 'Can't translate this page' (400) for every /c/ and /product.html URL tried, meaning Google's own fetcher was blocked there too. r.jina.ai returned explicit 403 Access-Denied text for both category and product URLs. Only WebFetch got past the interstitial layer far enough to read page title/branding (though it still hit the site's own 'There was an error processing your request' state rather than a product grid) - which is what produced evidence signal #4 above.

No rows are extracted here because there is no genuinely separate Overstock Home Decor catalogue to extract - it is the same catalogue as S.N. 47, and re-listing it under a second S.N. would double-count identical categories/quantities already recorded in c47.json.
